reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess target engagement for either RO7247669 (TLR9) or tiragolumab (TIGIT). Cannot determine if compounds reached their intended targets. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess downstream biology changes. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed results across arms - some arms showed success (nivo+ipi 77.3% pRR, RO7247669 mono 80% pRR) while others showed partial (RO7247669+tiragolumab 60% pRR in neoadjuvant, atezolizumab+tiragolumab 45% pRR) or failure (RO7247669+tiragolumab 0% ORR in advanced cohort). The combination appears less effective than monotherapy. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Different cohorts (neoadjuvant vs advanced) showed different responses, with advanced cohort failing completely. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Multiple arms with different endpoints (pRR vs ORR) make direct comparison difficult. Safety signals include serious cardiac events (myocarditis, myocardial ischemia) and immune-related AEs.

failure_modes.evidence: RO7247669 monotherapy showed 80% pRR success in neoadjuvant setting, but combination with tiragolumab showed reduced efficacy (60% pRR partial, 0% ORR failure in advanced). Different populations responded differently.
